findings.location: source.html — Scripture list (first <ul> of verses near start)
findings.source_quote:
• Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Ephesians 5:33.
  • Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands… –1 Peter 3:1.
  • Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are… –1 Peter 3:6.
  • Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord –Ephesians 5:22.
  • But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God –1 Corinthians 11:3.
  • Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression –1 Timothy 2:11-14.
  • Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be [subject] to their own husbands in every thing –Ephesians 5:24.
  • Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law –1 Corinthians 14:34.
findings.suggested_fix:
These are quoted Scripture passages from the authoritative English source but remain in English in the translation. Quoted Scripture must be translated into Modern Standard Arabic while preserving the exact chapter and verse numbers and the number/placement of references. Replace each English verse text with an accurate Arabic rendering of the cited verse(s) (using conventional Arabic book names such as أفسس, بطرس الأولى, كورنثوس الأولى, تيموثاوس الأولى, عبرانيين if applicable). Keep the verse citations (e.g., —أفسس 5:33) and any emphasis (, ) in the same HTML positions and tags. Do not substitute a different Bible version; render the printed English meaning faithfully into Arabic. Example fix for the first item:
  • ولذلك لتَرَ المرأة أن تُجِلَ زوجها —أفسس 5:33.
    • (Translate all items similarly.)
findings.translation_quote: Same blocks preserved verbatim in the translation (English Scripture text remains) — e.g., “Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Ephesians 5:33.”

findings.location: source.html — Embedded Scripture passages later in body (Titus and 1 Peter blocks)
findings.source_quote:
تيطس يُعطينا أخوات توجيهًا واضحًا من الله. The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

...

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement [terror]. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.
findings.suggested_fix: These embedded, quoted Scripture passages remain in English in the translation. Translate the quoted Bible text into Modern Standard Arabic, including bracketed glosses (e.g., [conduct], [modest, innocent…], [terror]) into Arabic. Preserve the original HTML tags, emphasis (, ), and the exact verse references (e.g., —تيطس 2:3-5; —بطرس الأولى 3:1-2 و 3:6-7). Do not alter verse numbers or omit any clause. For example, replace the Titus English quote with a faithful Arabic rendering of Titus 2:3-5 in the same … element. Likewise translate the 1 Peter block fully into Arabic and keep the bracketed glosses translated and in brackets.
findings.translation_quote: Both the Titus quote and the 1 Peter passage are left in English inside … in the translated article (e.g., “The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; … –Titus 2:3-5.” and the long 1 Peter quotation).

findings.location: source.html — Aside (Romans quotation and bracketed notes)
findings.source_quote: Wherefore, as by one man [not one woman] sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned … Nevertheless death reigned from Adam [not from Eve] to Moses, even over them [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race] that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression… –Romans 5:12-14.
findings.suggested_fix: The Romans quotation remains in English; additionally the bracketed clarifications (e.g., [not one woman], [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race]) are in English. Translate the quoted Scripture into Arabic, and translate the bracketed explanatory material into Arabic as well, keeping them in brackets and in the same place. Preserve the verse numbers (—رومية 5:12-14) and the emphasis tags. Example: لذلك، كما بخطيئةِ إنسانٍ واحدٍ دخلت الخطيئة إلى العالم، وبالخطية كان الموت، وهكذا انتقل الموت إلى جميع الناس، لأن الجميع أخطأوا … ومع ذلك سواد الموت من آدم [وليس من حواء] إلى موسى، حتى على الذين لم يخطئوا بمثل عصيان آدم… —رومية 5:12-14.
findings.translation_quote: The translation currently contains the entire Romans quotation in English inside the aside.

findings.location: source.html — Bible book names and verse citations throughout
findings.source_quote: Multiple occurrences such as “–Ephesians 5:33.”, “–1 Peter 3:1.”, “–Genesis 2:18.”, final aside parenthetical “(see 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Romans 13:12)”
findings.suggested_fix: Book names and verse citations appear in English in many places. Conventional target-language (Arabic) book names should be used for citations (e.g., أفسس for Ephesians, بطرس الأولى for 1 Peter, تكوين for Genesis, كورنثوس الأولى for 1 Corinthians, رومية for Romans). Replace the English book names with their standard Arabic equivalents while keeping the exact chapter:verse numbers and any parenthetical references unchanged. Example: change “–Ephesians 5:33.” to “—أفسس 5:33.” and “(see 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Romans 13:12)” to “(انظر كورنثوس الأولى 11:3 ورومية 13:12)”.
findings.translation_quote: The translation leaves the English book names and verse citations as in the source (e.g., “–Ephesians 5:33.” and “(see 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Romans 13:12)”).
